diagnostic_evidence.quote: By Proposition~\ref{prop:convergence_iterative_surrogate}, the inequality~\eqref{eqn:proof_thm_2} achieves equality only when $\theta\left(\mathcal{F}\left(\bm{Q} \bm{z}_k^{(j+1)}\right)\right) = \theta\left(\mathcal{F}\left(\bm{Q} \bm{z}_k^{(j)}\right)\right)$ except at the zero entries of $\bm{d}_k$ or at the zero entries of $\mathcal{F}\left(\bm{Q} \bm{z}_k^{(j+1)}\right)$ for all $k=1,2,\dots,N$.

issues.failure_explanation: The theorem asserts an equivalence (if and only if) between the objective values matching across successive steps and the new iterate being a critical point. The reverse implication is false: if an iteration steps from a non-critical point to a critical point with lower objective value, $\nabla_{\bm{z}}\Phi(\bm{z}^{(j+1)}) = 0$ holds while $\Phi(\bm{z}^{(j+1)}) < \Phi(\bm{z}^{(j)})$. Furthermore, the proof in Appendix B.2 only argues the forward implication and provides no justification for the reverse implication.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Weaken the equivalence in Theorem 3.2 to the forward implication $\Phi(\bm{z}^{(j+1)}) = \Phi(\bm{z}^{(j)}) \implies \nabla_{\bm{z}}\Phi(\bm{z}^{(j+1)}) = 0$, or characterize stationarity in terms of $\bm{z}^{(j)}$.
issues.overall_effect: The bidirectional equivalence asserted in Theorem 3.2 is invalid in the reverse direction.
issues.title: False bidirectional equivalence in surrogate optimality characterization
issues.why_classification: Weakening the equivalence to a one-directional implication preserves the necessary guarantee (stationarity upon convergence) with no downstream loss or proof architecture changes.

issues.failure_explanation: For any bin $r$, the coarse maximum evaluates to the reciprocal of the arithmetic mean of $v = \bm{u} + |\bm{Q}|^2$ across the bin, while the fine maximum evaluates to the arithmetic mean of the reciprocals $1/v$ across the bin. By the AM-HM inequality, the average of reciprocals is strictly greater than the reciprocal of the average unless all entries in the bin are identical. The proof in Appendix G invalidly asserts that restriction commutes with reciprocal inversion, claiming $\bm{I}_h^H(1/v) = 1/(\bm{I}_h^H v)$.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the equality with an inequality $\max_{\|\bm{g}_1\|_\infty\le 1} |\bm{e}_{H,k}(\bm{I}_h^H\bm{g}_1)|_r \le \max_{\|\bm{g}_2\|_\infty\le 1} |\bm{I}_h^H\bm{e}_k(\bm{g}_2)|_r$, which holds by Jensen's inequality and still shows that the coarse update magnitude is controlled by the fine update magnitude.
issues.overall_effect: Proposition 4.3 as stated is mathematically false for any non-constant probe or regularization pattern.
issues.title: False equality between coarse and fine regularization update maxima
issues.why_classification: A one-line local replacement of the equality with an inequality by Jensen's inequality preserves the substantive claim that the coarse update magnitude is controlled, with no dependent formal results affected.
